analysis.title: GS - Callahan - US TMT Apple AAPL Does It Get Defended or Not - 3 Nov 2026
key_insights: NDX futures were +65 bps pre-market as the NDX tried to bounce off its 200-dma after a ~275 bps intra-day roll the prior day. Crude was moving toward ~$100, and the prior day's oil decline helped only the consumer discretionary pockets of tech.

Overnight pre-market moves: SHOP -16%, DT -15%, ZBRA -14%, IT -7%, PLTR -6%. AAPL was -4% pre-market and was the biggest focus of the day as the largest company in the world and as a read on risk appetite.
Apple has become a proxy for anti-AI / NDX trading. If the dip is bought, it could indicate still-muted risk appetite for AI infrastructure and semis.

Top inbound client questions: whether PLTR gets defended, why ON rallied ~8% from its post-print lows, whether AI goes higher if Apple sells off, software issues (DT, NOW, ZS, TWLO), earnings set-ups (AMD, NET, DDOG, ANET, FWONK, LYV, OTAs), and continued drag in INTC and AMD.

Events today: US midterm elections, JOLTS data, SNOW Expedition 2026 CEO keynote at 1pm ET, WSJ Tech California Conference. Post-market earnings: ALAB, AMD, ANET, ANGI, BKNG, CPNG, DUOL, FLYW, FRSH, HURN, NVTS, OUST, PCOR, RVLV, SWKS, TOST, TREE, TRVG, XYZ.

Bull case on AAPL: topline trends better than expected (iPhone revenue +17% y/y in September, December total revenue guided +7-10% y/y), early days of a product cycle (Duo/foldable, touchable MacBook), and the bad news on gross margins and Services is already in the stock. iCloud+ could help re-accelerate Services over time. Capital returns and FCF yield remain strong, and Apple has privacy, distribution and scale advantages to eventually deliver AI to consumers.

Bear case on AAPL: mix-shift headwinds as high-margin Services decelerate (December quarter Services guided +8-9% y/y on mobile gaming softness, third-party licensing (TAC) headwinds, and App Store changes such as U.S. link-out transactions). Gross margin headwinds are emerging as lower-cost memory inventory and tariff-refund benefits fade. Server-side inference costs for Siri AI may be recognized in Services COGS. Apple's ability to compete in consumer AI tooling is still uncertain.

GIR (Mike) keeps AAPL at Buy. Estimates came down ~2% overnight (to ~$9 in FY27 and ~$10 in FY28) on margin compression from supply constraints. GIR has increased confidence in the iPhone refresh cycle, including a multi-year opportunity for iPhone Duo and the foldable form factor.
Valuation: AAPL forward P/E is ~35x versus ~19x for the NDX, a historically wide gap. AAPL's FCF yield relative to the NDX is on trend, with Apple offering a slightly better FCF yield.
Gross margin debate: whether FY26 is peak gross margin for Apple (including some one-time tariff refund benefit), or whether a Services re-acceleration can keep lifting corporate gross margin.

Positioning: AAPL is widely held, but GIR mutual fund positioning data shows a consistent underweight, and hedge fund conversations suggest lukewarm sentiment. Apple short interest is elevated but off its highs.
About 90 days earlier, after F3Q results, the AAPL dip was short-lived. Apple became negatively correlated to the NDX and traded more like a low-vol safe-haven proxy.

tension_points.bull_case: iPhone revenue +17% y/y in September and December revenue guided +7-10% y/y. The Duo/foldable and MacBook product cycle is early, the bad news on gross margin and Services is priced in, and capital returns and FCF yield remain strong. GIR keeps Buy.

GIR cut estimates ~2% on supply-constrained margins.
